svg.title: Azure Virtual Desktop in a hybrid environment
svg.desc: Not an official Microsoft diagram. At the top, the Microsoft-managed Azure Virtual Desktop service (control plane) with the web service, gateway service, broker service, resource directory and geographical or regional database, and Microsoft Entra ID. In an internet band, user devices running AVD clients sign in to Microsoft Entra ID and connect to the service over TLS. A customer Azure subscription holds a spoke virtual network with a session host subnet protected by a network security group and a host pool of session hosts running the AVD agent, a hub virtual network with a gateway subnet and an optional Azure Firewall subnet, VNet peering between hub and spoke, profile storage in Azure Files or Azure NetApp Files for FSLogix, and Azure Monitor with a Log Analytics workspace. The on-premises network holds Microsoft Entra Connect and domain controllers (AD DS). The hub gateway connects to the on-premises network by ExpressRoute or VPN. Session hosts connect outbound to the service (reverse connect). Microsoft Entra Connect synchronizes identities to Microsoft Entra ID.
svg.text: Azure Virtual Desktop in a hybrid environment
Azure Files or Azure NetApp Files
AD DS joined hosts need line of sight to domain controllers (here, via peering and the gateway); Entra joined hosts do not.
If you use a firewall, allow the required AVD endpoints and do not use TLS inspection.
User sign in, and connection to the service over the internet
Session host outbound connection to the service (reverse connect)
Private link between on-premises and Azure (ExpressRoute or VPN)
Private traffic inside Azure: peering and profile storage access
Logs and metrics sent to Azure Monitor
